text: A game that was super simple and not expensive. Started out using sprite assets that look pretty close to Castlevania things, and instead of seeking retribution, Konami joins up with two collabs with two DLC tributes to the fun of gaming while keeping it all affordable. This is pure gaming at it's finest: "Having fun over making money", I and every other gamer out there salute you for this.

Updated Review: 

This game was good when EA dropped, it is nearing great now. The art style is incredibly cool, the story is engaging, and the world itself is just awesome to explore. The combat is difficult to start, but satisfying to learn, and has a lot of range to it with all of the different weapon types. Exploration is worthwhile and the interconnected-ness of the world reminds me of dark souls 1. 

Just get it, you'll dig it.

Solid game. Nice aesthetic - very easy on the eyes. Good gunplay and movement. Great soundtrack to go along with gunning down enemies through linear maps. It is a fairly short game with only one game mode and a new game +. Small issue with ledging where it looks like you teleport up there sometimes if you land too low. The final fight for me was bugged pretty badly to where the boss wouldn't take any damage after a certain phase, but it worked after restarting a few times. Couldn't make heads or tails about the story, I didn't completely understand it and it doesn't seem like it was the main priority. It's a good FPS game in a cool cyberpunk world. I'd recommend buying it during a sale as 40 dollars is a bit steep for the amount of game you get, but what you do get is very fun and quite polished.

I completely understand why this game has been nominated for 'Game of the Year'.

I really liked Midnight walk. I found it to be a pretty great linear adventure through a uniquely handcrafted world, with an amazing soundtrack. If you rush you can probably complete the game in under four hours, to collect everything will likely set you back five or six. Overall a short game, but overall I found it to be excellent, and I would look forward to see what this developer makes next.

It's clear why Far Cry 3 became the blueprint for what the open world genre would become, even to the modern day. It may be missing some of the quality of life features we see in modern open world games, but even to this day, over 12 years after its release, Far Cry 3 remains a fantastic time and something I recommend all open world fans play. Far Cry 3 above all else feels authentic and its clear the developers had a great time making this game. The story is wild and crazy, the characters are full of life, the open world is vast and fun to traverse, and the game isn't afraid to get weird. REALLY weird. 

Overall a fantastic time, even 12 years later.

Playing on Goblin difficulty was a fun challenge. There are no saves and when you die you have to restart the level. I don't think you can quit and continue, I think you have to make it in one go. You'll be using every ammo and hp pickup you can find. Projectiles will hit you, there's no way around it. Achievements were a mix of level completion and a few secret locations. You'll need 2 playthroughs and the last level might break you on the hardest difficulty. If you try to run past enemies they'll follow you wherever you go, even if they're packed inside a car and you go inside a building!

Planet of Lana  is a delightful puzzle platformer with stunning dynamic deep backgrounds, masterful soundtrack and a fantastic story that borrows ideas from multiple sources. Gameplay mainly focuses on your interaction with your companion to solve puzzles and help avoid the menacing creatures that you will encounter on your journey. The game starts off slow but ramps up the action on the later half with several surprising sections including a thrilling chase sequence. The game is roughly 5 hours long, divided in 12 chapters each with unique environments and hidden shrines to find. Puzzles are on the easier side to ensure smooth progression through your journey. Give this game a try if you like simple puzzle platformers or you enjoyed similar games like  INSIDE  or  Planet Alpha . [9/10]

Loved the original, so even with the bad optimization warnings, I figured "how bad could it really be?"

Turns out, pretty awful. Around the 20 hour mark, performance completely falls off a cliff. The memory leaks are brutal, forcing me to constantly restart the game just to clear them and keep it playable.

The Z2 Extreme should handle this with zero issues, but bad optimization ruins the whole experience. Nostalgia isn't worth having to reboot every hour…skip it until they actually patch it.

Do not buy this game. You will buy it thinking there's no harm in trying it because it's only $15, then you wall fall in love with it. One day you will want to play it while on the bus, so you will buy it on your tablet. Then your tablet will die and you will buy it on your phone. Then your switch. Then your X-box. Then you buy it for your sister so she can play online with you. Then you realize you can have 4 online players, so you buy it for your boyfriend. And then your sisters boyfriend. And then you realize you have spent $200 and 500 hours on this $15 game. 

Zero Regrets.

I like its art and the music, but I find the controls infuriating, and some save points further than they should be in a game that takes its platforming so dead serious. Backtracking through challenging areas just because you missed one exit on the map makes me want to smash the nearest controller. If you accidentally miss your shortcut, you can also brace yourself for some much-disliked backtracking. Do not give me areas where you need less-than-a-second react time, and then spread my save points too far from the last checkpoint, and then make your controls less than pitch-perfect. It's a recipe for disaster, and no amount of crafty art and pretty music can save the game play.
